aiWorkflow.title: How I work with AI
aiWorkflow.intro: I code with AI agents (mostly Claude Code) every day, but with a method: I set the context, the rules and the spec; the agent implements step by step; and I verify with tests and real data before anything reaches production.

items.title: Context before code
items.text: Every repository has a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md with the architecture, the current state and rules the agent must follow: errors must stay visible (no silent catches or fallbacks that hide them) and nothing gets committed or pushed unless I ask.

items.title: Spec-driven development
items.text: With OpenSpec, every change starts as a proposal with a spec and a task list; the agent implements it step by step, and at the end it's verified and archived. One data repository alone has 16 changes managed this way.
items.evidence: OpenSpec · /opsx commands: new, apply, verify, archive

items.title: Skills with business knowledge
items.text: I give the agent domain knowledge as reusable skills: the canonical catalog of PostgreSQL tables, a data-quality expert and FastAPI conventions. That way it doesn't guess which table to use or how to name things.

items.title: A log and handoff for every session
items.text: Every session ends with a document saying what was done, what was verified, what's fragile and what's left. The next session, mine or the agent's, starts by reading it, so context isn't lost from one day to the next.
items.evidence: KamasMarket: 39 technical docs, 9 of them session logs and handoffs

items.title: AI proposes, I verify
items.text: Nothing reaches production without testing: CI tests, diff review and real orders with small amounts. In KamasMarket, the first real order exposed three bugs that were invisible in code review, which is why I test with real data.

kamasmarket.name: KamasMarket
kamasmarket.summary: A P2P marketplace in production for buying and selling a video game's virtual currency, with a Solidity escrow, on-chain USDT and fiat payments, and an AI support chat (DeepSeek) that looks up the user's real data.
description: KamasMarket is a person-to-person marketplace for buying and selling kamas (the currency of Dofus Retro). Buyers and sellers don't know each other, so the money stays in escrow until delivery is confirmed.

The backend runs on FastAPI/Starlette with several uvicorn workers. PostgreSQL on Supabase holds the catalog, orders, internal wallets and the admin panel. Payments come in as on-chain-verified USDT, through a Solidity escrow contract on BNB Smart Chain, or through fiat/crypto gateways (Wompi and NOWPayments).

An automated delivery worker takes paid orders from an authenticated HTTP queue, completes the delivery and reports evidence. The backend then releases the funds to the seller. The site also has technical SEO in three languages (hreflang, dynamic sitemap) and runs on a Linux VPS with Docker.

I also built AI-powered support: two DeepSeek agents with function calling, one for customers and one for the admin team, kept apart by design (different prompts and tools, never mixed). The customer agent walks people through buying and selling, explains how to set up a payout method, and looks up the orders, sanctions, payouts and refunds of whoever is chatting; when it can't solve something, it opens a ticket for a human. The admin agent answers business questions (sales, commissions, conversion funnel, payment health, escrow, stuck orders) with 26 read-only tools.

challenges.problem: With several workers, two simultaneous requests could charge for or reserve the same offer twice.
challenges.solution: Per-operation idempotency keys, row-locking transactions and unique constraints in PostgreSQL. A retry returns the same result instead of creating a duplicate.

challenges.problem: Neither side trusts the other to pay or deliver first.
challenges.solution: A Solidity escrow contract: USDT stays locked and is only released when the backend confirms delivery. Timeouts and disputes trigger a refund.

challenges.problem: Choosing a network: on-chain fees can eat the margin on small orders.
challenges.solution: I compared BSC (BEP-20) and Tron (TRC-20) costs and chose BSC for the escrow because of its EVM ecosystem and per-transaction cost.

challenges.problem: Getting organic traffic in three markets from one site.
challenges.solution: Language-prefixed routes, hreflang tags, a dynamic sitemap.xml and indexing in Google Search Console.

challenges.problem: An AI chat that reads real data can be manipulated into showing another user's information.
challenges.solution: The restriction lives in code, not in the prompt: every customer-agent tool receives the authenticated session's user, never one the model chooses. The customer agent also has no access to any admin tool.

challenges.problem: One day the main model left requests queued for hours without answering.
challenges.solution: A fallback model with a circuit-breaker pattern: if the main model doesn't answer within 20 s, traffic goes to the fallback for 5 minutes, then the main model is tried again.

challenges.problem: A load test showed the backend degrading at 15–30 concurrent connections.
challenges.solution: I raised the container limits, moved to 3 uvicorn workers with a shared Redis rate limit, and put the domain behind Cloudflare.

achievements: Live in production with real users at kamasmarket.com.

Every order has its own smart contract (BEP-20) that can only release the payment to the seller or refund the buyer; besides the kamas market, there's an item marketplace and a merchant mode with exact stat validation.
Zero duplicate charges thanks to idempotency and transactional locks.
15+ versioned SQL migrations (wallets, counter-offers, sanctions, multi-bot, security).
Telegram and WhatsApp notifications, plus Google sign-in.
Reproducible Docker deployment on a VPS with hardened SSH.
AI support in 3 languages: 34 tools (8 for customers, 26 for admins), human escalation through tickets, and every conversation logged as resolved, unresolved or escalated.
Chat usage limits: 20 messages per minute, 2,000 characters per message, history trimmed to 30 messages and at most 5 tool rounds per answer.
While building the agent, a contact-data leak in public endpoints and a bug that inflated the count of in-progress orders were found and fixed.
media: Live home page (kamasmarket.com): kamas and money offers, item marketplace and contract-protected purchases
Kamas and money offers with price per million, server and currency filters (usernames blurred)
Item marketplace with a game-style interface: exact item stats and protected purchase (seller blurred)
Help center: delivery, wallet payments, BEP-20 vs. TRC-20 network and recovering late payments

steps.title: The buyer picks an offer
steps.text: The site is served in the URL's language (/es, /en, /fr). The buyer picks a server, amount and payment method.

steps.title: Create the order, no duplicates
steps.text: The browser sends the order with an idempotency key. If the network fails and the user retries, FastAPI returns the same order instead of creating a new one.

steps.title: Reserve stock with a row lock
steps.text: Inside a transaction, PostgreSQL locks the offer so no other worker can sell it at the same time.
steps.code: SELECT … FROM offers WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE

steps.title: Payment arrives
steps.text: The gateway sends a signed webhook (fiat or crypto), or the backend verifies the USDT transfer on-chain with enough confirmations.

steps.title: Funds in escrow
steps.text: The USDT is locked in the escrow contract. Nobody can touch it until delivery is confirmed or the deadline passes.

steps.title: The worker claims the order
steps.text: The delivery worker polls an HTTP queue authenticated with a shared key and claims only paid orders.

steps.title: Delivery confirmed
steps.text: The worker reports delivery with evidence (amounts and buyer verified). If something doesn't match, the order goes to manual review.

steps.title: Release funds
steps.text: The backend releases the escrow and credits the net amount to the seller's internal wallet, which they can withdraw at any time.

steps.title: Notify both sides
steps.text: Each user gets a notification on Telegram or WhatsApp, whichever they prefer.

steps.title: Ask the chat
steps.text: From any page, the buyer opens the support chat. It answers in the page's language and walks them through the process: how to buy, how to set up a payout method, what each step means.

steps.title: Real data, only theirs
steps.text: If they ask about their order, the model calls a tool (function calling) that queries the database filtered by the session's user. If it can't solve the issue, it opens a ticket for the team.

cruces-interinstitucionales.name: Inter-agency data cross-check
cruces-interinstitucionales.summary: A web system that queries 8 public data sources in parallel from a single ID number, reads image captchas with Gemini Vision and streams progress live with Server-Sent Events.
description: A team of analysts had to log into 8 government portals one by one (health insurance, social programs, traffic, business registry, social security and notary records) to cross-check each case. Each lookup took several minutes.

I built a FastAPI app that runs all 8 lookups in parallel. Each scraper runs in its own thread with its own headless Chromium browser (Playwright), with per-source retry settings and parsers that turn different formats into one. Three of the portals show an image captcha: Gemini Vision (Vertex AI) reads it and, if the reading fails, the scraper retries with a fresh captcha.

The browser gets live progress for each source through Server-Sent Events. At the end, the result is saved to PostgreSQL and a Word report is generated in the official format. It ships as a Docker container on GCP and as a desktop installer.

With use, the app grew to 8 modules: single lookups (8 ID document types, including PEP, PPT and refugee safe-conduct); batch lookups from CSV or Excel that can resume without repeating people, start from scratch, or only download missing evidence PDFs; RUNT lookups by plate and owner; vehicle market value from FASECOLDA by VIN; Word report generation from the database, single or in batch, without querying the portals again; an Excel evidence matrix (one row per person, yes/no per source); a mode that reads requests from Google Sheets, queries only what's missing and uploads the PDFs and cross-check form to Google Drive; and a Gemini usage dashboard with daily quota and cost projection. It also handles multiple Supernotariado accounts.

challenges.problem: Portals are slow and unreliable; one source going down blocked the whole check.
challenges.solution: One thread and browser per source, per-source timeouts and retries with backoff (3 to 10, depending on the source). If one fails, the others keep going and the report marks what's pending.

challenges.problem: Analysts couldn't tell whether a lookup was still running or had hung.
challenges.solution: SSE event streaming: each source reports 'queued', 'running', 'done' or 'error', and the UI updates without reloading.

challenges.problem: Every portal returns data in a different format (HTML, tables, PDF).
challenges.solution: One parser per source with a shared output schema, so the report and the database don't depend on the portal.

challenges.problem: Some users' machines couldn't run Docker.
challenges.solution: Two ways to ship it: a container on GCP and an .exe installer (Inno Setup) with a system tray icon.

challenges.problem: Three portals (health, traffic and social security) show an image captcha on every lookup.
challenges.solution: The captcha image is sent to Gemini Vision on Vertex AI, which returns the text. If the portal rejects it, a new captcha is requested and the lookup retries (5 to 10 attempts depending on the source).

achievements: All 8 lookups run at the same time instead of one after another by hand.
8 modules in one app: single and batch lookups, RUNT by plate, FASECOLDA, Word report and Excel matrix from the database, Google Sheets and Drive integration, and an AI cost dashboard.
Custom Gemini usage dashboard: 1,361 captcha readings in 30 days for US$0.24, with 98.4% successful lookups on RUAF and 99.4% on RUNT, and 1.1 to 1.7 calls per lookup.
Live progress for each source, with clear statuses for the analyst.
Word reports generated automatically in the official format.
Author of 50 of the repository's 55 commits.
media: Single lookup: document type and number, and selection of the 8 sources (no personal data shown)
Batch lookup from CSV or Excel: resume without repeating people already checked, download evidence PDFs and save to disk
Custom Gemini usage dashboard: calls, tokens and cost per source and per day (1,361 calls in 30 days for US$0.24)

steps.title: The analyst enters an ID
steps.text: They type the number and pick the sources to query. (All data in this portfolio is fictitious.)

steps.title: Create the job, open the stream
steps.text: FastAPI replies right away with a job id, and the browser opens an SSE connection to follow progress.

steps.title: 8 lookups in parallel
steps.text: The orchestrator starts each source in its own thread with an isolated headless Chromium. If one hangs, the rest aren't affected.

steps.title: Automated browsing
steps.text: Playwright opens the portal, fills in the form and waits for the result. On timeouts or network errors it retries with backoff.

steps.title: Captcha with Gemini
steps.text: If the portal shows an image captcha, it's cropped and sent to Gemini Vision (Vertex AI), which returns the text. If the portal rejects it, a new one is requested and the lookup retries.

steps.title: Normalize results
steps.text: Each parser turns the portal's HTML or table into a shared schema.

steps.title: Partial result to the orchestrator
steps.text: Each source returns its result as soon as it finishes, without waiting for the others.

steps.title: Live progress
steps.text: FastAPI emits an SSE event on every status change, and the UI shows each source's progress.

steps.title: Save the check
steps.text: The combined result is saved to PostgreSQL with asyncpg for auditing and later queries.

steps.title: Generate the report
steps.text: The official Word template is filled in and the analyst downloads it.

agente-ia-territorial.name: Territorial AI agent
agente-ia-territorial.summary: A Claude-powered agent that runs statistical and spatial analysis on Medellín data and writes HTML reports with charts, with full tracing and metrics.
description: An agent that answers questions about the city (neighborhoods, districts, addresses, business activity) with real analysis, not just generated text.

It uses the Anthropic SDK with a tool-use loop. Claude chooses among 8 tools (data profiling, geocoding, spatial, temporal, statistical modeling, risk validation, address analysis and narrative), and Python runs them with pandas and GeoPandas and sends back the results.

Domain knowledge is organized into 'skills' (business diagnosis, territorial analysis, visualization and reporting). The output is an HTML report with Plotly charts, and the whole run is traced with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus.

challenges.problem: LLMs make up numbers when you ask them to do statistics directly.
challenges.solution: All calculations go through deterministic Python tools. Claude only orchestrates and interprets, and every number in the report comes from a tool.

challenges.problem: Colombian addresses are written in many different ways ('Cra 43A # 1-50', 'KR 43 A 1 50').
challenges.solution: An address normalization and validation tool runs before geocoding and flags doubtful records.

challenges.problem: There was no visibility into how much each agent run cost or how long it took.
challenges.solution: OpenTelemetry traces for every tool and model call, plus token and latency metrics exported to Prometheus.

achievements: 8 reusable analysis tools with clear input and output contracts.
Automatically generated HTML reports, ready to share.
End-to-end observability: every agent step can be traced.
A skills architecture that adds new domains without touching the core.
media: Comparative dashboard generated by the agent: KPIs, top 10 districts and breakdown by type (fictitious data)
Ranking with percentage distribution and cumulative share by district (fictitious data)

steps.title: A question arrives
steps.text: For example: 'Which districts have the most food businesses, and how did that change over the last year?'

steps.title: Load the right skill
steps.text: The agent detects the domain (business diagnosis) and loads its instructions and examples.

steps.title: Ask Claude
steps.text: The question is sent along with the definitions of the 8 tools (name, description and JSON schema).

steps.title: Claude picks a tool
steps.text: The response comes back with stop_reason = tool_use, naming the tool to call and its parameters.

steps.title: Run it in Python
steps.text: The agent actually runs the tool: deterministic calculations, no made-up numbers.

steps.title: Analyze the data
steps.text: pandas and GeoPandas join the records with district boundaries and compute the statistics.

steps.title: Send the result back
steps.text: The result goes back to Claude as a tool_result. The loop repeats until the model has what it needs to write the answer.

steps.title: Build the report
steps.text: An HTML page is built with the write-up and interactive Plotly charts.

steps.title: Measure everything
steps.text: Every model and tool call leaves a trace with its latency and token count.

bot-trading.name: ML algorithmic trading system
bot-trading.summary: 3 active bots running in parallel with machine learning models validated by walk-forward testing and statistical tests, 25,000 predictions logged to SQLite, and a custom web panel to control them and audit every trade.
bot-trading.role: Author (ML, backend, analysis and web panel)
description: It started as a simple bot and grew into a full algorithmic trading lab on top of a broker's API (forex and crypto). Three bots run in parallel, each with its own supervisor and a watchdog that restarts the connection if the API hangs.

At its core is a gradient boosting model (scikit-learn) trained on 16 technical indicators and validated with walk-forward testing: it's trained on the past and evaluated only on data it has never seen. An edge is accepted only if its win rate beats the breakeven point, 1 / (1 + payout), with a significant permutation test.

Everything goes into SQLite: every run, every prediction (traded or skipped) and every trade with its latency and actual payout. To visualize and analyze the results I built a statistics web panel from scratch (a Python HTTP server of about 5,200 lines, JavaScript and hand-built SVG charts): for each bot it shows the win rate against breakeven, the P&L curve, max drawdown and streaks, filters by period, exports to CSV, starts and stops bots, and draws a chart of each trade with what the bot saw when it decided. Results are measured against breakeven, not raw P&L. Every strategy goes through three stages: a backtest on historical candles (January to November 2026), a practice account and, only if the results hold up, a real-money account. Today only ETH 5m (stochastic) trades with real money, and it matches what its backtest showed. ETH 5m RSI and BTC 5m are still on practice.

challenges.problem: A backtest showed an 11-point win-rate boost that didn't actually exist.
challenges.solution: I found the bias: the backtester counted ties as wins. Since then, every strategy is checked first against the raw market's base rate.

challenges.problem: I needed to know whether the model's confidence filter actually improved anything or just cut the number of trades.
challenges.solution: The panel compares the win rate of traded vs. skipped signals ('is the threshold useful?') and shows why the bot didn't trade in each case. If skipped signals win as often as traded ones, the filter isn't selecting anything.

challenges.problem: Many 'winning' strategies on historical data were pure luck.
challenges.solution: Anti-self-deception rules: win rate against breakeven, permutation tests and time-based splits. That's how I discarded, over 7,022 simulated trades, a Weis Wave + Bollinger strategy that looked good (47.6% win rate).

challenges.problem: The API sometimes hung with no timeout, leaving the bot 'alive' but without data.
challenges.solution: A watchdog that kills the hung call, and supervisors that restart each bot independently.

challenges.problem: A bug cut progression cycles one step short.
challenges.solution: I rebuilt the real cycle candle by candle (forensic analysis), measured what the bug cost and fixed it.

achievements: 2 edges validated with walk-forward testing: EUR/USD 15 min (55.6% win rate, p = 0.0006) and BTC/ETH 15 min (56–58%), above the 52.6% breakeven.

ETH 5m (stochastic) now trades on a real-money account: 60.7% win rate (17 wins, 11 losses) against a 54.9% breakeven at the actual payout received (82%), in line with its backtest on historical data (61.1% over 2,091 trades).
Backtests on historical candles from January to November 2026 (simulated, not executed trades): ETH 5m RSI 58.2% over 4,395 and BTC 5m 56.7% over 6,109. Both trade on practice accounts today.
25,240 predictions and 749 trades logged with full traceability (January to November 2026).
10 models and strategies evaluated; those that failed the statistical test were dropped before scaling up.

A statistics web panel built from scratch (Python with no framework, about 18 REST endpoints, JavaScript and custom SVG charts): win rate against breakeven, P&L curve, max drawdown, streaks, P&L per day and per asset, period and time-zone filters, CSV export, multiple accounts, 5-second refresh, in Spanish and English. Shareable over an SSH tunnel.
Packaged with Docker, a Windows installer and a licensing system.

steps.title: Validate before trading
steps.text: Each model is trained and evaluated with walk-forward testing. It only goes to production if it beats breakeven with a significant permutation test.

steps.title: Real-time candles
steps.text: The broker delivers closed candles. If the call hangs, the watchdog kills it and the supervisor restarts the bot.

steps.title: Compute indicators
steps.text: The bot computes 16 indicators (RSI, stochastic, CCI, ADX, MACD, Bollinger, ATR…) and asks the model for a probability.

steps.title: Is it worth it?
steps.text: The probability is compared with the confidence threshold and with the breakeven for the current payout.

steps.title: Order
steps.text: If it passes the filter, the order is sent. Each bot has its own mode: ETH 5m trades on the real account; the rest stay on practice until their backtest proves itself.

steps.title: Log everything
steps.text: The prediction (traded or skipped) is saved, along with the trade's latency, actual payout and result.

steps.title: Audit
steps.text: The panel groups results by model and draws a chart of each trade with what the bot saw.

steps.title: Control
steps.text: Bots and accounts are started and stopped from the panel, without touching the console.

bot-ruleta.name: Live OCR automation
bot-ruleta.summary: A desktop automation that reads live results with double-checked OCR, runs a configurable strategy and logs everything: 329 sessions and 740 spins analyzed.
description: An automation for a live roulette table: it reads the strip of results on screen with OCR, applies a configurable pattern strategy and clicks on the interface.

The interesting part is the engineering around it. Each number is isolated by cell, binarized and confirmed twice (pixel color and OCR) before it's used. There are per-resolution screen profiles with a guided calibrator, 'dry' (watch only) and 'visual' (moves the mouse without betting) modes, a timetable-based scheduler and a web stats panel.

The log analysis confirmed what theory says: the martingale wins almost every cycle (335 of 337), but the 2 long losing streaks wipe out all the gains. I keep this project as a computer-vision exercise, and as a lesson in measuring with data before trusting a strategy.

challenges.problem: Red numbers on a dark background and the 0 on green confused the OCR.
challenges.solution: Per-cell segmentation, binarization (white on black) and dilation, plus a second check against pixel color. If they disagree, another capture is taken.

challenges.problem: Coordinates changed with every monitor and resolution.
challenges.solution: JSON screen profiles, a guided calibrator and a tool that compares the configured positions with the real screen.

challenges.problem: Testing without risking anything.
challenges.solution: 'Dry' and 'visual' modes, plus a command that verifies the clicks before running for real.

achievements: 329 automated sessions and 740 spins logged to CSV.
509 readings confirmed by a double check (pixels + OCR), with no unresolved conflicts.
Multi-resolution profiles with guided calibration.
Analysis on real data: 335 of 337 cycles won and still a net loss, evidence that the martingale creates no edge.
media: OCR pipeline: the original strip (top), segmented by cell and binarized (bottom)
Hard cells: the number is confirmed across 3 captures before it's accepted

steps.text: The scheduler launches the bot on its configured timetable and prevents duplicate processes.

steps.title: Load the profile
steps.text: The calibrated regions and coordinates for the current resolution are loaded.

steps.text: The results region is cropped from the screen.

steps.text: OpenCV cleans up the image, Tesseract reads it, and the result is validated.

steps.title: Decide and act
steps.text: The engine applies the strategy. In dry mode it only logs; in visual mode it moves the mouse without acting.

steps.title: Log

bot-mineria.name: Vision-based automation bot
bot-mineria.summary: A ~10,000-line desktop agent that runs a full gather-and-sell loop by only looking at the screen (46 templates, OCR and a state machine with a watchdog) and reports its status to Supabase.
description: A bot for a video game that uses no APIs and doesn't read memory: it makes every decision by looking at the screen, like a person would.

It finds elements with OpenCV template matching (46 templates) and pixel checks, reads prices with Tesseract, and runs a full loop: gather, go to the bank, sell at the market above a minimum price, and come back.

To run for hours unattended, it has a watchdog thread that restarts the game after 5 minutes without progress and detects disconnects and loading screens. Each PC also reports a heartbeat and its events to Supabase, so several machines can be monitored at once without ever blocking the main loop.

challenges.problem: The bot got stuck in odd states (disconnects, pop-ups).
challenges.solution: A safety function called inside every loop, plus a watchdog on a separate thread that forces a restart when there's no progress.

challenges.problem: A 10,000-line file that was hard to maintain.
challenges.solution: An architecture document with the overall flow and an index of functions by responsibility, as a first step toward splitting it into modules.

challenges.problem: Selling too cheap because of a misread price.
challenges.solution: Validated OCR and a per-resource MIN_PRICE: if it isn't met, the sale is blocked.

achievements: Runs for hours unattended and recovers on its own.
The full gather → bank → market loop is automated.
Fleet monitoring: each PC reports its status to Supabase (best-effort, never blocks the bot).
46 vision templates and 3 test suites (bank, market and functions), with documented architecture.
media: The 46 templates the vision system looks for on screen with cv2.matchTemplate

steps.title: Capture the screen
steps.text: The relevant region of the game window is grabbed.

steps.title: Recognize the state
steps.text: Template matching and pixel checks find where the character is and what's on screen.

steps.title: Act
steps.text: The state machine decides the next click or move.

steps.title: Read the price
steps.text: At the market, the current price is read with OCR.

steps.title: Validate the sale
steps.text: If the price is below MIN_PRICE, the sale is blocked.

steps.title: Self-recovery
steps.text: After 5 minutes without progress, the watchdog restarts the game and reconnects.

steps.title: Log
steps.text: Everything goes into a timestamped log for debugging.

steps.title: Report status
steps.text: A separate thread sends a heartbeat and events (disconnects, restarts) to Supabase. If there's no internet, the bot carries on unaware.
